html:
Most apartment move-outs in Greer come down to one afternoon: the movers leave, the keys are due, and the kitchen still has a drawer of crumbs and an oven nobody has opened in a year. If that sounds familiar, this guide covers what apartment move out cleaning in Greer needs to include, in the order a team actually works through it.

Greer sits across Greenville and Spartanburg counties (ZIPs 29650, 29651 and 29652), and renters here are scattered along I-85, SC-14 and US-29. The checklist is the same wherever you live, but the timing is not: a lease that ends on the last day of the month means everyone is booking the same few days.

What the move-out walkthrough usually looks at

Property managers differ, so read your lease and any move-out sheet they gave you. In a typical walkthrough, though, the spots that draw attention are the same ones we see ourselves when we walk into an emptied apartment: the inside of the oven, the refrigerator shelves and drawers, the bathroom grout, the tub edges and the floors along the baseboards. Smaller items get missed because they hide in plain sight, like the tracks of a sliding patio door, the tops of door frames and the inside of the cabinet under the kitchen sink.

A tenant is rarely judged on one dusty shelf. What costs people part of a deposit is a pattern: grease on the stovetop, a film on the shower glass, and hair along the floor edges all add up to a home that was not cleaned for the next renter.

What apartment move out cleaning in Greer should cover

Here is the room-by-room list our team works from. You can use it to clean yourself or to check what a cleaner has included.

  • Kitchen: inside and outside of every cabinet and drawer, inside the refrigerator and freezer, inside the oven and microwave, range hood, stovetop and backsplash.
  • Bathrooms: toilet base and behind it, grout, glass doors, tub and shower walls, and inside the vanity.
  • Bedrooms and closets: shelves, rods and closet floors, plus wiped doors, frames and light switches.
  • Windows: sills, tracks and blinds.
  • Floors: vacuumed and mopped edge to edge, which is the very last step.

The full list of what we do is on our move-out cleaning in Greer page.

Our move-in and move-out cleaning service is built around that walkthrough, so the checklist above is the same one the team follows. Because apartments are usually smaller, we can often finish in a single visit, but we confirm that at the estimate.

The order matters more than the effort

Renters who clean on their own often work hard and still end up redoing the floors. The reason is sequence. Dust and crumbs fall, so you start high and finish low. Lights, vents and the tops of door frames come first. Cabinets, appliances and counters come next. Bathrooms follow, and floors always go last, backing out toward the front door so you are not walking on a wet floor.

The oven is the other place people lose time. If it has baked-on grease, a few minutes of spraying will not do it. Our Brazilian detail-first method is to let the product sit while we move on to another room, then come back and finish. That is a small habit, but it is the difference between one pass and three.

Some renters find that a place left in rough shape needs a deep cleaning level of effort before the move-out checklist even starts. We will tell you that during the estimate rather than after.

How much does apartment move out cleaning cost in Greer?

There is no honest flat number, because two apartments with the same floor plan can be very different jobs. What moves the price is the home size (rooms and square feet), the condition the last occupant left it in, how much the oven and refrigerator need, whether the place is empty or still has furniture, and how tight your timing is. A key return due tomorrow morning may need a bigger team than a move-out with a week to spare.

You can book it with the form on the page above, by calling (864) 399-5168 or by texting (864) 666-8520. If you want to see how the numbers are built for a house, our post on move-out cleaning for Landrum renters goes through a similar checklist, and you can also use the estimate form on our home page.

Cleaning it yourself versus hiring a team

QuestionDoing it yourselfHiring a team
TimeUsually a full day or more after the moveA crew handles the whole list, often within one visit
Oven and refrigeratorEasy to leave half doneIncluded in the move-out service
SuppliesYou buy and carry themBrought by the team
Deposit riskDepends on how thorough you areDetail work done in a set order

Many renters in Greer split the difference: they pack, haul and clear out the trash themselves, then book apartment cleaning in Greer for the kitchen, bathrooms and floors, which are the slowest parts. That keeps the cost of hiring help focused on the jobs that eat the most hours. Neither choice is wrong. If you have help, a free weekend and an apartment in decent shape, doing it yourself can work. If you are working until the day before the lease ends, a team saves you the worst of it.

How long it takes and booking this week

A small, tidy apartment takes a team a few hours. A larger one, or one with heavy grease or hard water buildup, takes longer. We will not guess before seeing the place. If your move is this week, book the estimate right away, since the last days of the month fill up first. For anything beyond the apartment, including a house you are listing, our move-out cleaning in Taylors page covers the same service just down the road.

When you are ready, book your free estimate for move-out cleaning in Greer and tell us your key return date.
